speaker: richard_field
text: Sit by the fire. The wine is Jacqueline's, and the cups were on the oak before you came, so do not thank the press for them. What hast thou brought me that is not a chronicle?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Pages. Not a play. A dozen leaves, no title, and no last act. I am going to read, and I am not going to pretend the pile is finished because it is thick enough to warm a hand.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Read, then. If both of you begin on paper prices I will take the cups away. Non. I came for the page, not for a quire.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Workmen, rehearsing in a wood. A weaver correcting them. Then the man who mends the bellows, and the line is in a voice that will have to be a girl's. Most radiant Pyramus, most lilly white of hue.

speaker: richard_field
text: I had a straight face for the casting. I have lost it. Thou hast put all Warwickshire into Athens, Will. Thistles, weavers, asses and moonshine. I shall wipe my eyes on my sleeve, and I am supposed to be a sober man.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Wipe them. The line is the line. I am not improving it because a printer laughed. He goes into the brake a man and comes back with the head, and he sings to show he is not afraid.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: And the queen. You said she wakes. Is she punished for loving an ass?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not yet. I haven't got that far.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Then don't.

speaker: richard_field
text: Hear her. A sentence of punishment would be doctrine, and I am suspicious enough of fairies without thee adding a homily. Leave the woman where she woke.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I left her there this morning. The blank under the question is the blank. I am not filling it to make a hearth more comfortable.

speaker: richard_field
text: Have they paid you? The three nights. I would rather have it plain.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No, not yet.

speaker: richard_field
text: Good. That is more useful than a flourish. An empty office is an empty office. Do not gild it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not gild it. The book at home still thinks it is this year. I am not writing a warrant I have not seen.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: A dozen leaves and no last act is an honest count. Do not let him round it, Richard. A round number is how a printer begins to promise a book.

speaker: richard_field
text: I am not promising a book. I am laughing at a bellows-mender, which is cheaper. Thou mayest leave the pages if thou wilt. I will not set them. A playhouse can have them when thou hast an end, and I am not that playhouse.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not leaving them to be set. They go home in the same fold. The chronicle does not come with me tonight either. It is on my shelf, and it is staying through the new year.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: A dozen, and no title. Say the number once and leave it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A dozen. No last act. I have said it.

speaker: richard_field
text: At the door, then, since thou art standing. Is the second volume of my Chronicle to see the new year in Great St Helen's?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is.

speaker: richard_field
text: God keep thee, then, and it.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: God keep you both, and the cups. I will wash them. You will not help, either of you, because helping is how a man stands in a kitchen telling the plot again.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have told it. She wakes. She is not punished. A dozen, and no last act. Good night.

speaker: richard_field
text: Good night. Feel the fire on the way out if you must. It is sea-coal, and it will not follow thee to Bishopsgate. The page might. Do not let the page become fair by being tired of it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is not fair, and I am not tired of it in that way. I am going before I write an ending to please a washbasin.
